explanations.a: Backup configuration is only useful if restoration works.
explanations.b: Per-resource assignments do not scale; assign at the resource group, subscription, or management group instead.
explanations.c: A query of activity logs does not back up data; create a backup job in a Recovery Services or Backup vault.
explanations.d: Management groups are about org-wide policy and access at scale; billing rolls up via subscriptions.

questions.name: Deploy and manage Azure compute resources
questions.text: A workload owner asks the Azure administrator to implement configure App Service backup. Which option should be selected?

answers.text: Use a single VM in place of a Virtual Machine Scale Set for elastic web traffic
Protect the backup storage account with appropriate access controls and retention settings
Use Network Watcher Connection Troubleshoot as a packet-capture utility
Use Azure Backup without ever performing a restore drill

explanations.a: VMSS adds/removes instances based on demand; a single VM cannot scale out and is a single point of failure.
explanations.b: Backups can contain sensitive application data and configuration.
explanations.c: Connection Troubleshoot tests reachability and returns next-hop info; full packet capture is a separate Network Watcher feature.
explanations.d: Untested backups are theoretical; periodic restore drills validate that recovery actually works.
